prompt_context: Draft an Application for Suspension of Sentence under Section 430 BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 389 CrPC) before the appellate court. Section 430 BNSS empowers the appellate court to suspend the execution of the sentence or order appealed against pending appeal, and if the convict is in confinement, release him on bail or on his own bond. The application must establish: (1) particulars of conviction and sentence; (2) filing/intent to file appeal; (3) prima facie arguable case (without inviting merits adjudication); (4) likelihood of long delay in appeal disposal; (5) no flight risk; (6) willingness to furnish bond. Key precedents: Atul Tripathi v. State of U.P. (2014) 9 SCC 177; Vijay Kumar v. Narendra (2002) 9 SCC 364; Kashmira Singh v. State of Punjab (1977) 4 SCC 291 (long-pending appeal — bail ordinarily granted). Use BNS for substantive offences, BNSS for procedural sections.
promptInstructions: Draft an Application for Suspension of Sentence under Section 430 BNSS, 2023 (successor to Section 389 CrPC).
Set out particulars: trial court, case number, date of judgment, offences and sentence.
Confirm that Criminal Appeal has been filed (or is being filed simultaneously) — application not maintainable without an appeal.
Brief outline of grounds of appeal showing arguable case — but do NOT pre-judge merits.
Emphasise that appeals routinely take 3-5+ years to be heard, and continued detention would render the appeal infructuous.
Cite Kashmira Singh v. State of Punjab (1977) 4 SCC 291 on suspending sentence where appeal not likely to be heard for long.
Cite Atul Tripathi v. State of U.P. (2014) 9 SCC 177 on principles for suspension of sentence.
Reference convict's antecedents, social roots, family responsibilities.
Use BNS section numbers for offences of conviction (never IPC).
Do NOT generate the verification clause or advocate signature block — those are added programmatically.
